stages.title: Prologue
stages.goal: Finish Gone Fishing and learn the controls it teaches.
stages.note: Nothing is missable yet. Use the mission as a tutorial: Combat Focus, cover and the partner commands all come back later.

stages.title: Chapters one to four
stages.goal: Play the story missions, take every dialogue choice, and pick up one of each activity type on the way.
stages.note: Six chapter and mission trophies plus Actions Speak Louder land here. Save manually at the start and end of every chapter.

stages.title: The missable window
stages.goal: Close every character strand, the stranger strands and the one-off encounters while they still exist.
stages.note: The description ties these to a character's final mission, a unique target or a single scene. This is the stage that decides whether the platinum is still reachable.

stages.title: The finale
stages.goal: Finish the last story mission for the gold.
stages.note: The point of no return. Do not start it until stage three shows nothing open.

stages.title: Collectibles and exploration
stages.goal: Sweep the map: meditation spots, card sets, WAiNK check-ins, vehicle discovery and every named area.
stages.note: Nothing here closes, so it is the calmest stage. One district per session beats one trophy per session.

stages.title: Activities, races and one-offs
stages.goal: Stunts, drone races, the shooting range, the arcade, bowling, the airport and the showroom.
stages.note: The long grinds. Cunning Stunts and the shooting range are the two that take real hours; do them in blocks of one activity type.

stages.title: Jobs, combat and money
stages.goal: Rob everything, fight everything, launder the proceeds and buy every garage.
stages.note: Income first: the bank vaults and gang operations pay for Little Boxes and Treat Yo Self.

stages.title: 100% and the platinum
stages.goal: Close the completion checklist for A Long Road, and take the platinum it unlocks.
stages.note: The percentage is the game's own audit of everything above. Whatever is still missing is the last gap in the pause menu breakdown.

trophies.guide: This is the receipt for the other fifty-four, not a task of its own: it unlocks the moment the last one lands, so the only plan that matters is the plan for everything else. Treat it as a progress bar you cannot push directly. It will not appear early no matter what you do, and it will not appear at all if a single missable strand closed before you finished it, so the real work is protecting the windows listed under Missables.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: The opening mission, and the tutorial for driving, cover and the weapon wheel all at once. Play it straight the first time: it teaches the controls you will lean on for the next fifty trophies, and rushing the shooting section is how most people arrive at chapter one with no idea how Combat Focus works. It pops on the closing cutscene, not on the last kill, so do not reload to check.
steps: Finish the intro without skipping the tutorial prompts; they unlock the mechanics later trophies rely on.
Let the mission's cutscene play out; the trophy fires at the end of it.
Save manually the moment you are back in free roam — that save is your chapter-zero checkpoint.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: A chapter gate: it fires when the last mission of chapter one finishes, whatever order you did the missions in. Nothing in the chapter can be failed permanently, so the useful habit is not chasing this trophy but using chapter breaks as save points. Keep one manual save at the start of every chapter and a second at its end; the endgame cleanup is much calmer when you can step back a chapter instead of a whole story.
steps: Play chapter one's story missions in any order; the trophy waits for the last one.
Save manually at the chapter's first and last mission.
While in chapter one, try one of each activity type for Master of None — they are all close to the starting districts.

trophies.guide: A named story mission inside the chapter run, so it arrives on its own if you play the story. The name is the only clue the list gives about where it sits, so tick it when it lands rather than hunting for it. There is no fail state that removes it: a mission you fail can be replayed from the retry screen or the mission replay menu, and the trophy fires on the first successful completion.

If you fail it, retry from the pause menu rather than reloading a save — the trophy only needs one completion.

trophies.guide: The last of the named story missions before the finale, and the one most likely to be somebody's first death in a scripted chase. trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The second gold, and the one trophy that quietly depends on all the others: the percentage is the game's own checklist of story, strangers, hobbies, collectibles and random events, and a strand you let close early is a permanent hole in it. Open the pause menu's completion breakdown and work from the smallest number first — the last two or three percent is almost always one collectible set or one activity type you never tried. Do it after the credits, when nothing is gated.
steps: Open the pause menu's completion breakdown and note every category below 100%.
Close the smallest gap first; the last percent is usually a single set or activity.
Keep the platinum for last — this gold is the gate it waits on.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: The biggest single number on the list. Stunts are the map's jump markers, and each one counts once, so this is a sweep, not a grind you can shortcut by repeating a favourite ramp. Work district by district with the map filter on and tick them off as you land them; a jump that ends in a crash still counts if the game registers the landing. Leave it until the story is done and the map is quiet.
steps: Turn on the stunt filter on the world map and zoom to one district at a time.
Land each marker once; do not re-run one hoping for a second tick.
Keep a tally per district in the tracker's counter so a 250-item sweep stays honest.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: The cheapest trophy on the list and the easiest to forget: you only have to try one of each activity type, not finish any of them. The types are the map's own categories — races, drone races, fishing, the shooting range, the arcade, bowling, hunting, meditation and the stunt markers. Start one of each in the first two chapters and it is done before the story is halfway.
steps: Open the map's activity filter and note each distinct icon type.
Start one of each type; you can quit as soon as it begins.
Tick them off in the tracker so the last one is not a guess.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Forty-two range challenges, each needing a gold rather than a pass. Gold is a score threshold, so the route is repetition on one weapon at a time rather than a tour of all forty-two: learn a weapon's recoil pattern and its reload window, gold its challenges, then move on. Do the range late, with the best version of each weapon unlocked, and expect the timed ones to be the last two or three.
steps: Do one weapon category at a time; finish its golds before switching guns.
Prioritise accuracy over speed on the timed challenges — the clock is usually generous, the score is not.
Come back at the endgame with upgraded weapons for any stragglers.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Drone racing, and the trophy wants a win at each location rather than a finish. Fourteen of them, so treat it as fourteen short time trials: fly the route once to learn the gates, then race it properly. The drone handles badly at full throttle — feather it through the tight gates and save the boost for the straights. Losing a race costs nothing but the two minutes it takes to fly it again.
steps: Do a practice lap of each location before racing it for the win.
Feather the throttle through gates; full boost only on straights.
Win each of the fourteen, tracking them by location on the roadmap page.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: One cabinet, one full playthrough. Pick the shortest game in the arcade rather than the one that looks most fun: 'complete' means reaching the end, not a high score, and some cabinets are twenty-minute runs while others are three. If a cabinet's continues reset the run, finish it on one credit; if they do not, keep feeding it until the end screen appears.
steps: Play each cabinet once to see which is shortest.
Finish the shortest on as few credits as the cabinet allows.
Stay to the end screen — the trophy wants the completion, not the score.
